++++
+title = "4-axis and 5-axis machining"
+description = "Indexed and simultaneous multi-axis work: what CamCraft does for each kind, how to set it up, and what is checked."
+sort_by = "weight"
+weight = 8
++++
+
+Multi-axis machining adds rotary axes to the three linear ones. This section
+covers the four kinds of multi-axis work, what CamCraft does for each, what
+you set up, and what it checks before a program posts. It describes the
+program on `main` and says plainly where a feature does not exist yet.
+
+| Kind | The rotary axes | What CamCraft calls it | Page |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 4-axis indexed (3+1) | One rotary turns to a fixed angle, then 3-axis cutting | A tilted plane (3+2) with the A angle only | [Indexed work](@/guide/multi-axis/indexed.md) |
+| 5-axis indexed (3+2) | Two rotaries hold a fixed orientation, then 3-axis cutting | A tilted plane (3+2) with A and B | [Indexed work](@/guide/multi-axis/indexed.md) |
+| 4-axis continuous | One rotary turns while cutting | Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset | [Continuous 4-axis](@/guide/multi-axis/continuous-4-axis.md) |
+| 5-axis simultaneous | All axes move together | 5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, Swarf, Advanced Swarf, 5-Axis Flow, Multi-Axis Rough, Multi-Axis Contour | [Simultaneous 5-axis](@/guide/multi-axis/simultaneous-5-axis.md) |
+
+Read first [Machines, kinematics and TCP](@/guide/multi-axis/machines-and-tcp.md):
+which machine file you mount decides what is allowed, and the post you pick
+decides whether tilted moves post at all. The list of
+[checks](@/guide/multi-axis/checks.md) says what is refused and what only warns.
+
+## Machines that ship with a rotary axis
+
+Of the machine files in `assets/machines/`, four state a rotary axis. Every
+other shipped machine is 3-axis (or a lathe).
+
+| Machine file | Rotary axes | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| `doosan-dnm.mch` (Doosan DNM 5700) | A about X, travel stated as 360000 degrees | A table. Pairs with `doosan-dnm.cps`. |
+| `tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` (Tormach 770MX + microARC 4) | A about X, -360 to 360 degrees, `nose_to_axis` 10.6 | A table. Pairs with `tormach.cps`, which indexes A only. |
+| `tilthead.mch` (Tilt-head 5-axis) | A about X and B about Y, each -120 to 120 degrees, carrying the head | Head-head tilt. The 5-axis machine in the set. |
+| `millturn.mch` (Multitasking 5-axis) | C about Z, -360 to 360 degrees | Mill-turn; a C axis tilts nothing. |
+
+To add a rotary to your own machine file, follow
+[`docs/MACHINE-ONBOARDING.md`](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/main/docs/MACHINE-ONBOARDING.md):
+state the rotary part with its `axis` direction, its `travel` in degrees, and
+(for a table that turns the work) its `nose_to_axis`.
+
+## Related pages
+
+- The per-operation reference for the multi-axis operations is in
+  [Multi-axis operations](@/guide/operations-multiaxis.md).
+- What each machine type means for setups and operations is in
+  [Machine types](@/guide/machines.md).
+- If a post is refused, see [Reading a refusal](@/guide/refusals.md).

@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
++++
+title = "Checks on multi-axis work"
+description = "Reach and travel, the tilt tolerance, tool and holder collision, index swing, and what is refused or only warned."
+weight = 5
++++
+
+Anything a check flags as unsafe blocks the post. The checks below run for
+multi-axis work. Each says what it covers and what it does not.
+
+## Machine check: reach and travel per axis
+
+Before a program posts, the machine check judges the cached moves of every
+operation against the mounted machine's file, one sentence per problem. For
+tilted and rotary moves it says:
+
+- the move tilts the tool but the machine states no tilting rotary;
+- the move commands a rotary letter the machine states no axis for;
+- the commanded angle is outside that rotary's travel (it prints the range);
+- a lone rotary about X cannot reach the pose, judged through the tool axis;
+- a spindle C turn on a machine with no C axis, or outside its travel.
+
+A machine that states no travel for an axis is not checked for it ("the
+unstated-limit law"). Check your machine file's numbers against the machine's
+manual. If the problem count passes the report cap, the rest is counted.
+
+## Tilt tolerance
+
+The reach laws treat a tool as upright when its tilt off +Z is within 1e-9
+radians (`UPRIGHT_TILT_RAD`), so a move tilted only by float noise (about
+1e-10 degrees, as a rotated setup can produce) is judged as upright and does
+not raise a false holder collision (issue #938). A real tilt larger than that
+takes the tilted-tool path.
+
+## Shank, holder and fixture collision
+
+Along tilted moves the verifier reads the tool's shank and holder against the
+uncut stock and the part, and the fixture bands against the tool, at the
+pose of each move. A hit is reported as a shank hit (once per move). Shank
+avoid on the 5-axis operations moves the pose off such a hit within the Max
+tilt cone before it is reported.
+
+## Index swing
+
+Before a work-turning rotary (a table A or B) indexes, the post retracts the
+tool to the machine's safe Z. The post gate then checks that the tool tip at
+that height clears the radius the stock, parts and workholding that turn
+with the rotary sweep about the rotary's line, by a margin of 5 mm. Too
+little clearance refuses the post by name.
+
+- It needs the rotary's `nose_to_axis` (the distance from the spindle
+  nose to the centreline at safe Z) in the machine file. An unstated or
+  invalid value refuses, because the gate cannot show the turn clears.
+- It judges a level rotary line (A about X, B about Y). A vertical one
+  (C) keeps every height. A leaning line refuses by name.
+- It does not apply to a rotary that carries the head (a tilt-head).
+
+**Known gap (#1107):** the check judges the tool against the swept work. It
+does not judge the swept work against what stands still beneath it: the
+machine table, a fixture plate or a rotary subplate. A long or wide
+workpiece on a low rotary can swing into the table or plate and the program
+still posts. Check that clearance yourself.
+
+## Refused or only warned
+
+| Condition | Result |
+|---|---|
+| Tilt on a machine with no tilting rotary | Refused (machine check; also each non-TCP post) |
+| Rotary angle outside the machine's travel | Refused |
+| Post with no RTCP output given a tilted move | Refused by the post, counted warning, blocks the post |
+| Index swing clearance too small, or `nose_to_axis` unstated | Refused by name |
+| Shank or holder in the part or stock | Warning that blocks the post |
+| Stock simulation of a posed program | "Not judged", by name: the column engine cannot judge a tilted tool, so no pass is claimed |
+| Spindle body against the work, swept work against the table | Not checked |

++++
+title = "Continuous 4-axis: rotary operations"
+description = "Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset: finishing and roughing a turned shape on a rotary."
+weight = 3
++++
+
+In continuous 4-axis work the rotary turns while the tool cuts. In CamCraft
+this is the three **Rotary** operations (Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and
+Rotary Offset), which machine a shape of revolution such as a shaft or a
+cam blank. Their settings, defaults and refusals are in the
+[Multi-axis operations](@/guide/operations-multiaxis.md) reference; this page
+covers what the reference does not: how the axis meets the machine, feed, posts
+and a worked recipe.
+
+## How the axis is found
+
+You do not state the rotary's position. The generator fits the axis of
+revolution from the model's mesh. A mesh with no axis of revolution is
+refused by name, and the message points at the 5-axis operations; a part
+standing on its axis is pointed at Rotary Contour from Rotary Parallel and
+back.
+
+The fitted axis then has to match a rotary the mounted machine states. If
+the machine file lists rotaries with directions and none lies on that line,
+the operation is refused by name. The letter that posts is the machine's: A
+on the Doosan DNM or the microARC 4 file (A about X), C on `millturn.mch`.
+If the machine states no rotary directions, nothing is checked at
+generation and the machine check at post catches it.
+
+So the model must be placed so its axis lies along the rotary's line. On an
+A table the axis goes along X.
+
+## Feed on a rotary move
+
+The feed is written as a plain F word. CamCraft has no inverse-time feed
+mode (G93) in its shipped posts, so a move that turns the rotary does not
+get a degrees-per-minute or inverse-time conversion from the post. Where the
+machine file states a rotary's rate, the machine check judges the move
+against it, and `fanuc-lathe.cps` refuses a C-axis rapid when the machine states no C rate. On a
+control that wants inverse-time feed for simultaneous moves, the posted
+program is not ready for it as it stands.
+
+## Posts for continuous rotary moves
+
+Only posts with TCP output write a rotary that changes while cutting:
+`fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps`. `tormach.cps` refuses an A that changes
+inside an operation. The others refuse any tilt. See
+[Machines, kinematics and TCP](@/guide/multi-axis/machines-and-tcp.md).
+
+## Checks
+
+The rotary operations run a radial field check: the cutter's band against
+the fitted skin, the stock and the part, for gouges. A mesh imported coarser
+than promised gives its excess back from the allowance, and past that the
+operation is refused. The stock is the setup's stock solid.
+
+## Recipe: finishing a shaft on an A table
+
+1. Mount the Doosan DNM or microARC 4 machine, and its post.
+2. Import the shaft with its axis along X, and place the work offset on
+   the rotary's centreline.
+3. Add **Rotary Offset** to rough: set the radial **Stepdown** and the
+   top and bottom stations.
+4. Add **Rotary Contour** with the ball tool, tolerance 0.05, lead and
+   lag at zero.
+5. Run both and read the refusals, if any. Post with the Doosan post.
+
+## Not implemented
+
+- Wrapping a 2D drawing (engraving text or a pattern) around a cylinder.
+  Engrave and Trace cut flat planes; no operation unrolls a drawing onto a
+  rotary.
+- A stated rotary position: the axis comes from the mesh.
+- Inverse-time feed.

++++
+title = "Indexed work: 3+1 and 3+2"
+description = "Turn the rotary to a fixed angle, then cut with ordinary 3-axis operations."
+weight = 2
++++
+
+Indexed work keeps the rotary axes still while the tool cuts. The tool or
+the part is held at one orientation for the whole operation, so the cut
+itself is ordinary 3-axis work. Use it for several faces of one part in one
+setup, for reaching an angled face, and for shorter tools on deep features.
+
+CamCraft has one control for both kinds: the **Tilted plane (3+2)** group on
+a planar operation. It is not a separate machine mode.
+
+## Setting it up
+
+1. Mount a machine file with the rotary you need (see the
+   [shipped list](@/guide/multi-axis/_index.md)).
+2. Add a planar operation. These accept the tilt: Face, 2D Contour,
+   2D Pocket, Slot, Trace, 2D Adaptive, Offset 2D, Engrave, 2D Chamfer
+   and Circular. Drilling, the 3D and multi-axis operations, turning,
+   Trochoidal Slot, Probe and Plasma do not carry one.
+3. In its properties tick **Tilted plane (3+2)**. Set **Tool axis A** and
+   **Tool axis B** (degrees) and the **Plane origin** X, Y and Z (the point
+   the cut plane is anchored at, in world mm). A is limited to -90..90 and B
+   to -180..180 at command creation; anything else is refused. C is left to
+   the machine.
+4. Every move of the operation holds that one pose. The operation's picks,
+   offsets and boundaries are read in the tilted plane, with the plane's own X
+   and Y.
+
+Each operation carries its own tilt, so one setup can hold several indexes:
+set a different tilt on each operation. Changing the tilt is an ordinary
+undoable parameter edit.
+
+**3+1** is a tilt with A set and B at zero on a machine with one A table
+(`doosan-dnm.mch`, `tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`). **3+2** sets both A and B
+on a machine with two rotaries (`tilthead.mch`).
+
+## The work offset at each index
+
+On a machine with a table rotary, the work offset is placed in the
+setup frame, and the indexed post turns the table about the rotary's
+centreline. `tormach.cps` writes its tilted path in the indexed frame, so the
+work offset's Y0 and Z0 must lie on the A centreline; it says so in a note
+at the first index. The index swing check makes the same assumption: the
+WCS origin sits on the rotary's line.
+
+How an index posts depends on the post:
+
+- `tormach.cps` writes A alone, as `G0 A..` after a retract to the machine's
+  safe Z, at the start of a section. It writes no A word on a cutting move. It
+  refuses a B or C tilt, an A past the stated travel, an A that changes
+  inside an operation, an arc under a tilt (a tilted path is chords) and
+  a tilt on a machine with no A about X.
+- `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps` with `machine.rtcp` true arm `G43.4` and
+  write the angles (see [Machines, kinematics and TCP](@/guide/multi-axis/machines-and-tcp.md)).
+- Other posts refuse the tilt.
+
+## What is checked
+
+- The machine check at post: a tilt on a machine that states no tilting
+  rotary, an angle outside a rotary's travel, and a pose the machine's only
+  rotary cannot reach are each named and block the post.
+- Control-side cutter compensation does not ride a tilted 2D Contour: choose
+  **In computer**.
+- Tool shank and holder against the part and fixtures along tilted moves.
+- The index swing: see [Checks](@/guide/multi-axis/checks.md).
+
+## Recipe: a three-sided block, 3+1
+
+On a machine with an A table (for example the Tormach microARC 4 file).
+
+1. Clamp the block on the rotary and place the work offset on its
+   centreline.
+2. Op 1: 2D Pocket or Face on the top, no tilt (A0).
+3. Op 2: copy it, tick **Tilted plane (3+2)**, A = 90, B = 0, and set the
+   Plane origin to the point on that face.
+4. Op 3: the same with A = -90.
+5. Run each operation, then Post.
+
+The tilt letters stop at +-90 degrees, so an index reaches the top and the two
+sides, not the face opposite the top. For that face, flip the part: set the
+setup's part alignment to **Flip over X** in a second setup. (A part
+alignment is supported on Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket and 2D Adaptive.)
+
+## Recipe: an angled hole, 3+2
+
+CamCraft's Drill operation carries no tilt, so a hole off the vertical is
+cut as a circle: on a machine with a tilt-head, add a **Circular** operation
+(a circular pocket about a stated centre and radius), tick **Tilted plane
+(3+2)**, set A and B so the tool axis runs along the hole, set the Plane
+origin on the hole's entry point, and set the depth. A drilling cycle at an
+angle is not implemented.
+
+## Not implemented
+
+- Tilted drilling cycles.
+- Judging a tilted program in the stock simulation: a posed program is
+  reported "not judged" by name rather than judged as if the tool stood
+  vertical. The reach and shank checks above still run.

@@ -0,0 +1,83 @@
++++
+title = "Machines, kinematics and TCP"
+description = "Table-table, head-head and tilt-head machines, which axis limits apply, and what each post does with tilted moves."
+weight = 1
++++
+
+## What a machine file tells CamCraft
+
+The machine file's `parts` tree states every axis in the order it moves. A
+rotary part carries an `axis` direction (the line it turns about), a
+`travel` in degrees, and the parts below it. Three things follow from it:
+
+- **Does the machine tilt the tool?** CamCraft answers this geometrically. A
+  machine can tilt if some rotary states a direction that is not the Z
+  column. A C table (axis along Z) tilts nothing. A rotary with no stated
+  direction counts as tilting nothing: capability is claimed, never assumed.
+- **Does the rotary turn the work or the tool?** A rotary with the head
+  below it in the tree turns the tool; one without turns the work. The
+  [index-swing check](@/guide/multi-axis/checks.md) applies only to work-turning
+  rotaries.
+- **Which limits apply?** Each rotary's travel is judged per move, and the
+  linear axes are judged against their own strokes.
+
+## Table, head and tilt-head machines
+
+- **Table-table or table-only (a trunnion or a 4th-axis table).** The rotary
+  turns the work. In the shipped set this is `doosan-dnm.mch` and
+  `tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`, each with one A table about X. The
+  part sits on the rotary, so the work offset must lie on the rotary's
+  centreline (see [Indexed work](@/guide/multi-axis/indexed.md)).
+- **Head-head or tilt-head.** The rotaries carry the spindle, so the part
+  stays still. `tilthead.mch` is this: A about X, then B about Y, then the
+  head, each limited to -120..120 degrees.
+- **Mill-turn.** `millturn.mch` has a C axis about Z. It is a spindle
+  rotary for live-tool and rotary work, not a tilt.
+
+Why it matters:
+
+- **Reach.** The pose has to be inside every rotary's travel, and the
+  linear moves inside their strokes. A tilt-head with +-120 degrees cannot stand the
+  tool at a pose 150 degrees from vertical.
+- **Which limits apply.** A machine whose only rotary is about X is judged
+  through the tool axis: a stated pose such as A0 B180 reads as its A180.
+  Every other machine is judged letter by letter: an A trunnion asked for a B
+  turn is refused by name, since CamCraft never solves for another axis
+  combination.
+- **Singularities.** CamCraft does not solve inverse kinematics: the
+  generators state the tool axis and the post (or the control) turns it into
+  angles. A pose where two rotaries line up (tool straight along an axis) is
+  where a real control swings an axis fast. CamCraft has no singularity
+  check of its own; prove the program out in the control's own simulation.
+
+## TCP, RTCP and no TCP
+
+TCP (also called RTCP or TCPM) is the control's mode where the programmed
+point is the tool tip, and the control moves the linear axes to keep the tip
+on the path while the rotaries turn. Without it, the program has to contain
+the compensating linear moves, and CamCraft's posts do not compute those.
+
+The post reads `machine.rtcp` from the machine file (true when a rotary
+states a direction off Z) and does the following:
+
+| Post | Tilted moves |
+|---|---|
+| `fanuc.cps` | With `machine.rtcp` true, arms `G43.4 H<tool>` once per tool and writes the rotary words, modally. Refuses (counted warning, post blocked) a tilt on a machine with no tilting rotary, a letter the machine states no rotary for, a tilt inside a canned-cycle group, and a lone rotary stated along -X. |
+| `doosan-dnm.cps` | The same `G43.4` path when `machine.rtcp` is true. When it is false, a no-TCP path indexes an A table only: it needs rotary clamp and unclamp codes declared by the machine or post options, and refuses B or C words. |
+| `tormach.cps` | No TCP. A table about X is indexed between operations and A never changes inside one. See [Indexed work](@/guide/multi-axis/indexed.md). |
+| `haas.cps`, `heidenhain.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `sinumerik.cps` | Refuse every tilted move: these posts have no RTCP output. |
+| `carvera.cps` | Refuses every tilted move: the post is 3-axis. |
+| `fanuc-lathe.cps`, `tormach-lathe.cps` | Lathe posts; `fanuc-lathe.cps` handles C-axis live-tool sections, and refuses A/B words. |
+
+A refused tilt is a counted warning that blocks the post, so it cannot slip
+into a file silently.
+
+### When your control has no TCP
+
+If the control has no TCP, use only indexed work (3+1 or 3+2) with a post that
+indexes. Do not post simultaneous work to it. Known gap (#950): on the
+no-TCP path of `doosan-dnm.cps`, the post assumes A0 at the start of the
+program and after a tool change, so an A0 section writes no A word even
+though the table may stand elsewhere. Until that is fixed, start every program
+and every tool with an operation that moves A explicitly, or check the posted
+file for the missing A word.

@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
++++
+title = "5-axis simultaneous"
+description = "Swarf, flow, contour and roughing with the tool axis moving: lead, lag and the tilt limit."
+weight = 4
++++
+
+In simultaneous 5-axis work the part stands still and the **tool axis moves**
+on every move, while the linear axes follow. CamCraft has seven operations
+for it (5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, 5-Axis Flow, Swarf, Advanced Swarf,
+Multi-Axis Rough and Multi-Axis Contour), all in the **Multi-axis** group.
+Each operation's settings, defaults, lead, lag, max tilt, shank avoidance
+and refusals are in the
+[Multi-axis operations](@/guide/operations-multiaxis.md) reference. This page
+covers what that reference leaves out: what the machine and post must offer,
+the checks, and a recipe.
+
+## What it needs
+
+- A machine that tilts in two directions: `tilthead.mch` is the only shipped
+  file with two tilting rotaries. The Doosan and microARC 4 files have a
+  single A table, which can reach a pose only in the plane across A; the
+  machine check refuses a pose it cannot reach.
+- A post that writes TCP: `fanuc.cps` or `doosan-dnm.cps`. Every other
+  shipped post refuses a tilted move, so a 5-axis program does not post
+  with them. There is no 5-axis post for Heidenhain, Siemens, Haas or Mazak
+  yet.
+
+## Checks
+
+See [Checks](@/guide/multi-axis/checks.md). In short: the machine check judges
+the posed moves against rotary travel, the leaning-tool reach laws judge the
+shank and holder against the part and fixtures, and the stock simulation
+does not judge posed programs.
+
+## Recipe: finishing a ruled wall with Swarf
+
+1. Mount `tilthead.mch` with `fanuc.cps` or `doosan-dnm.cps`.
+2. Import a part with a ruled wall (a bladed or tapered side wall).
+3. Add **Swarf** with a flat or bull-nose tool. Leave lead and lag at
+   zero, set Max tilt to 90, and leave **Stepover** empty so the tolerance
+   sets it.
+4. Run it. If the model is doubly curved, the refusal names it; use
+   **5-Axis Parallel** instead.
+5. Post, then read the machine check and any warnings before cutting.
+
+## Not implemented
+
+- Singularity detection or avoidance: CamCraft does not model what a
+  control does when a rotary passes through a pole.
+- Collision of the machine's own spindle and head body against the work.
+  Machine files can state a spindle body size, but no check uses it; the
+  checks cover the tool, shank, holder and fixtures.
+- Judging a posed program in the stock simulation.
